objectives: Blend /n/ with previously taught sounds to decode simple CVC words.
Read CVC words containing n in initial and final positions.
Use sound-by-sound correction when n is confused with a previously taught consonant.
concepts: CVC decoding combines known grapheme-sound relationships in sequence.
The new /n/ sound can be blended with known /m/, /s/, /t/, /a/ and /p/ patterns.
Accurate decoding requires attention to every phoneme.

definitions.definition: Combining individual phonemes smoothly to say a whole word.
A simple word with consonant-vowel-consonant structure.
Using grapheme-sound relationships to read a written word.

workedExamples: If nap is read as map, return to the first grapheme and compare /n/ with /m/.
commonMistakes: Adding an extra vowel between sounds.
revisionPoints: See → say sounds → blend → check → reread.

basic: Blend taught phonemes into CVC words.
conceptual: Explain how changing one phoneme changes the word.
higherOrderThinking: Select the sound to revisit when a word is misread.
mixedReview: Read m/s/t/a/p/n CVC words and contrast similar words.

weakTopicRevision: Practise one-sound contrasts before returning to full CVC blending.

outcomes: Learner decodes n-containing CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner reads n initially and finally with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner corrects common n/m and n/t confusions using sound-by-sound analysis.
Learner blends without adding extra vowel sounds.
